name: marketing
description: Campaign studio — research an audience, decide the message, pick channels, generate media in the right form factors, hand the operator a pack they publish themselves, and measure what came back.
author: Biffo Team

tables.name: marketing_campaign
tables.description: A campaign. Everything else in this plugin hangs off one of these, and its id is what `utm_campaign` carries — which is the whole point: attribution becomes a foreign key by construction rather than a string somebody typed.

columns.name: status
columns.description: draft | researching | planned | generating | ready | live | archived. Not an enum column — plugin tables have no enum type, and the service layer validates.

columns.name: brief
columns.description: What we want, for whom, by when. Free text; the agents read it.

columns.name: destination_url
columns.description: Where tracked links point. Configurable so installing into another instance is config, not a rewrite.

columns.name: media_kinds
columns.description: Comma-separated: copy,image,video,audio. Which media the operator asked for — drives which agents run, how long it takes and what it costs.

columns.name: guidance
columns.description: Shown beside the pack. Carries disclosure and music-licensing obligations, because whoever presses publish warrants them — and that is the operator, not us.

tables.name: marketing_artefact
tables.description: One agent-produced stage output — research, positioning, or channel plan — with its approval state. One table rather than three because the lifecycle is identical and the only difference is `kind`; three tables would triple the approval logic to keep in step.

columns.name: campaign_id
columns.description: Plain key, not a foreign key — plugin tables cannot declare FKs. Validated in the service layer.

columns.name: kind
columns.description: research | positioning | channel_plan

columns.name: status
columns.description: pending | proposed | approved | rejected

columns.name: body
columns.description: JSON-serialised. Plugin tables have no JSON column type, so structured artefacts are Text.

columns.name: citations
columns.description: JSON-serialised source list. Separate from body so 'this claim has no source' is a structural question, not a prose one — a research run that cites nothing must be detectable without reading the prose.

columns.name: causation_id
columns.description: The agent chain that produced this. Joins to agent_runs, which is how per-campaign LLM spend is assembled — caller_plugin alone under-reports fan-in.

tables.name: marketing_asset
tables.description: A piece of generated creative, stored via Core's plugin object storage. The bytes live in S3; this row is the record.

columns.name: media_kind
columns.description: image | video | audio

columns.name: placement
columns.description: feed_1x1 | portrait_4x5 | story_9x16. The form factor this rendering is for.

columns.name: media_id
columns.description: Core plugin-media id. The URL is minted per request and never stored — a stored URL is stale the moment it is written.

columns.name: is_source
columns.description: True for the one approved creative; the placements are DETERMINISTIC RENDERS of it, never regenerations. Nullable, treat NULL as false — a declared default reaches the model but not the migration DDL.

tables.name: marketing_link
tables.description: A tracked link: campaign x channel x variant. Its token is what makes `utm_campaign` a real reference rather than a hopeful string.

columns.name: token
columns.description: secrets.token_urlsafe(32). Never echoed into a response body, event payload or log line.

columns.name: channel
columns.description: e.g. linkedin, instagram, email

columns.name: variant
columns.description: Which creative variant this link is attached to.

columns.name: destination_url
columns.description: Resolved at mint time with UTMs stamped, so a later campaign edit cannot rewrite a link already published.

columns.name: is_paid
columns.description: Organic or paid placement. Nullable, treat NULL as false.

tables.name: marketing_click
tables.description: One click on a tracked link, recorded by Core's public redirect BEFORE the 302. Append-only; never updated. This is the only pre-submission server-side event in the whole funnel — the intake pages are static exports, so nothing else can observe a visitor before they submit a form.

columns.name: campaign_id
columns.description: Denormalised so per-campaign click counts need no join.

columns.name: user_agent
columns.description: Truncated. No IP address is stored: it is personal data we have no use for, and not collecting it is cheaper than justifying it.

tables.name: marketing_channel
tables.description: The channel taxonomy (#67, #76 increment 1): a closed, admin-extensible vocabulary of stable channel ids, replacing the free-text `channel` strings that let a 121-character agent-generated name overflow `marketing_link.channel` (#75). `key` is the stable, machine-safe identifier a future `ChannelRecommendation`/`ChannelCopy`/`marketing_link` will reference (#76 increment 2, not this table) — it plays the role the manifest's auto-injected `id` (a Core-generated UUID) cannot, since that is neither short nor stable across a re-seed. Nothing here is platform-, vertical- or tenant-specific: this plugin installs on every Biffo platform, and the taxonomy is deliberately broad (digital and offline/field) rather than encoding any one operator's vocabulary.

columns.name: key
columns.description: Stable machine-safe identifier, e.g. 'google_search_paid'. Short by construction — every seeded key is well under this column's 64-character ceiling — so the #75 overflow class cannot recur through a channel referenced by key rather than by a hand-typed name. Relabelling must never change this: it is what a future recommendation/copy/link row will reference, and changing it under an existing reference would silently break the join it exists to make structural.

columns.name: label
columns.description: Operator-facing name, e.g. 'Google Search ads'. May be long and descriptive — this is the field an operator reads; `key` is the field code and storage join on. Splitting the two is what makes #75's overflow impossible rather than merely unlikely: the field that can be long is never the field that is stored short.

columns.name: motion
columns.description: organic | paid. Lives on the channel, not only on a recommendation: 'Google Search ads' is inherently paid, and LinkedIn-organic/LinkedIn-paid are different channels with different work attached, so this is a property of what the channel IS rather than something an agent asserts independently each time. Plain String — plugin tables have no enum type.

columns.name: category
columns.description: One of: search, social, video, email, content, communities, partner, events, trade_press, direct_mail, local_field (#67's taxonomy shape). Groups channels for display; not itself referenced by any other table.

columns.name: ad_platform
columns.description: Optional. The ad platform this channel's spend and character limits belong to (e.g. 'google', 'meta', 'linkedin', 'tiktok'), NULL for channels with no platform-specific limits (organic search, direct mail, events, ...). Exists now so the shape a future `_platform_for_channel` lookup needs (replacing today's substring guessing) does not require a second schema change — the lookup itself is #76 increment 2, out of scope here.

api_routes.description: List campaigns for the caller's tenant.
List artefacts for the caller's tenant.
List assets for the caller's tenant.
List links for the caller's tenant.
List clicks for the caller's tenant.
List the channel taxonomy for the caller's tenant. Readable by any authenticated caller — the operator selection UI (#67) and the seed script both need it.
Add a channel (admin only) — used by the default-taxonomy seed script and by an instance adding its own channel.

Relabel, recategorise or reassign a channel (admin only). `key` is not editable through this generic route in practice — nothing calls it — but Core does not restrict which columns a generic update may touch, so this is a documented convention, not an enforced one.
Remove a channel (admin only). A future recommendation/copy/link row that already referenced this channel's key would be orphaned, same trade-off as idea-scout's business-model categories.

event_subscriptions.description: Example subscription: logs newly created users. Replace with real logic, or remove this block if your plugin doesn't need it.
